sth_hermit_fan.text: Helier the hermit lived out on that rock and is said to have prayed all day while the pirates were coming. They put him to the sword, but not before he'd finished.
Check the tide table before you cross. Folk have been caught out on the causeway. The sea doesn't come in, it just stops going out and you suddenly realise.

sth_crapaud.text: Jerseymen are called crapauds, which means toads. Nobody can quite agree why. There are plenty of toads, and plenty of theories.
Guernsey folk are called donkeys, ânes, some say for their steep streets and some say for their stubbornness. Sark's lot are crows. We've all got a name, and we've all been quietly insulted.

sth_langtry.text: Lillie Langtry was born at St Saviour in 1853, the Dean's daughter. She became one of the most photographed women in England, an actress, a friend of the Prince of Wales and, I'm told, the owner of a racehorse called Merman.
Millais painted her holding a lily in 1878 and called it 'A Jersey Lily'. A lily, that is, not an actual lily. The name stuck to her for life.

st_helier_bureau.text: Jersey pounds are at par with sterling. Shops here take your English money gladly, but the change comes in Jersey notes, which England won't take back.
